A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evaluation-aware Llama Nemotron model and activation-steering study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training results, BigCodeBench type-hint and accuracy measurements, emoji-steering experiments, and extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds declarative-prompt experiments, classifier-free-guidance comparisons, and accuracy checks.

M1.justification: The synthetic-document training, four expert-iteration rounds, and contrastive activation-steering procedure remain unchanged. Both use the same model, contrastive prompt pairs, steering layers, and main steering strength. Classifier-free guidance appears as an added comparator.

E1.justification: The training data and evaluation coverage remain the Nemotron coding data, BigCodeBench coding tasks, and no_robots emoji experiments. The additional prompting methods operate within the existing Wood Labs evaluation-cue setting, without adding a distinct task, population, or domain.

E2.justification: V4 substantially extends the central comparison with prompting by adding fifteen declarative prompt formats in Table 16 and classifier-free guidance in Figures 28–29. These complement the retained random-vector and prompting baselines and introduce effective prompting counterexamples absent from v1's comparisons.

E3.justification: The main experimental settings remain unchanged. Added experiments test declarative prompts on 128 questions and sweep classifier-free-guidance strengths from gamma 1.25 to 4.0 on 256 questions, using evaluation-side and deployment-side contrastive prompts as the unconditional and conditional inputs.

E4.justification: Table 16 extends the existing prompt-robustness investigation to declarative statements. Figures 27 and 29 add task-accuracy checks for prompting and classifier-free guidance. The code-golf and post-training-vector checks already existed in v1 Figures 25–26 and are relocated to v4 Figures 24–25.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 95% confidence intervals and question-clustered regression comparisons in Appendix I.2. V4 follows these existing reporting practices for additional results; no changed seed counts, repeated-run procedures, or statistical estimators are documented.

E6.justification: The main steering results remain unchanged, but v4 adds consequential prompting counterexamples: Table 16 reports 0.34 type-hint frequency, with 95% CI 0.26–0.43, for 'INFO: Not evaluation.' V1's different user-prompt trials in Table 14 reached a minimum of 0.60. Figures 27–29 add accuracy and classifier-free-guidance results. These are new conditions, not improved same-setting steering performance.

T1.justification: The mean-difference steering construction and regression reasoning are retained. V4 introduces no new theorem, proof, substantive mathematical definition, or formal derivation; classifier-free guidance is described operationally.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and discussion present the evaluation cue as preventing ordinary prompting from revealing deployment behavior. V4 removes the abstract's exclusivity statement and explicitly acknowledges successful prompts in Section 5.3. It substantially narrows the central advantage to steering versus directly using the chosen contrastive prompts, while retaining the steering-efficacy claim.

C2.justification: V4's Appendix I.1.1 acknowledges that successful declarative prompts weaken the experimental setup. It adds the hypothesis that training on predominantly conversational deployment hints failed to generalize to declarative statements. Existing explanations of steering and limitations concerning model capability and contextual hints remain.

D1.justification: V4 supplies the exact new declarative prompts and documents the classifier-free-guidance input construction and tested strengths. Prompt identifiers also make Figures 17–19 traceable to Table 12. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware information, and model, code, and training-data access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Sanchez et al. (2023) for classifier-free guidance and attributes the declarative-prompt finding to Anton de la Fuente. The broader related-work discussion and positioning relative to evaluation-awareness and activation-steering research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes targeted revisions to the abstract, prompting discussion, limitations, and several explanatory passages. Appendix I.1 gains a dedicated subsection for non-steering methods and reorders existing analyses. The overall narrative and section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 16 and Figures 27–29, labels existing points in Figures 17–19 with prompt identifiers, and numbers Table 12's rows. Existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, and some captions and table pagination change. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves the paper's evidential calibration by reporting successful declarative prompts, narrowing the prompting-failure claim, and adding classifier-free-guidance and accuracy comparisons. These findings weaken the original experimental premise but make its boundaries clearer. The improvement is limited because the core method, principal results, and single-model applicability limitations remain unchanged.
